newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DODGERS, WITH LEFTY REYES DEBUTING, BEAT GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DODGERS, WITH LEFTY REYES DEBUTING, BEAT GIANTS.

text.p: Dennis Reyes, the Los Angeles Dodgers' first left-handed starter since 1992, struck out six over six innings in his major-league debut, a 9-3 victory over the first-place San Francisco Giants Sunday.
Los Angeles took 3-of-4 from the Giants to cut their lead in the National League West to four games.
Raul Mondesi's leadoff homer snapped a sixth-inning 3-3 tie. Todd Hollandsworth added a two-run single to cap the inning and give the Dodgers a three-run cushion.

The 20-year-old Reyes (1-0) was the Dodgers' first lefty starter since Bob Ojeda on September 24, 1992, a span of 681 games. Recalled from the minors on Saturday, he allowed three runs and four hits with four walks.
Reyes was coaxed out of the dugout for a curtain call by the Dodger crowd.
"This has never happened to me and I'll remember it for the rest of my life," he said.
"The first inning, I was very nervous, but after that, things worked out fine."
The rookie surrendered a first-inning homer to Barry Bonds but helped himself in the fifth when he drew a leadoff walk and later scored the tying run.

"We were very pleased, and I know he was," Los Angeles manager Bill Russell said. "But more than that, he was having a good time. He hung a slider to Bonds, who's supposed to hit those. It didn't rattle him. It's a big game today, it's a two game swing."
The Dodgers stopped Shawn Estes' eight-game win streak. Estes (12-3) gave up six runs and eight hits in five innings.
The Dodgers have won nine of their last 10.

In Cincinnati, Pedro Martinez pitched a one-hitter with nine strikeouts and Mike Lansing had a pair of triples, scored a run and drove in another before leaving with heat exhaustion as the Montreal Expos shut down the Reds, 2-0.
"I'll live," Lansing said. "I'm just a little tired. It wasn't real smart of me to hit two triples on the hottest day of the year."

Martinez (11-4) allowed only a one-out fisted bloop single by Bret Boone in the fifth. Martinez pitched nine perfect innings at San Diego on June 3, 1995, before allowing a leadoff double in the 10th.
Martinez tied Toronto's Pat Hentgen for the major-league lead with his eighth complete game and lowered his ERA to 1.62, also best in the majors.

Coming off a dominant one-inning stint in Tuesday's All-Star Game, Martinez notched his eighth straight start with at least nine strikeouts. During that span, he has fanned 90 in 66 2/3 innings. However, he is just 3-3 in that stretch.

In Atlanta, pinch-hitter Alex Ochoa homered with two out in the top of the 10th and Butch Huskey hit a pair of homers and drove in five runs as the New York Mets overcame a six-run deficit to defeat the Braves, 7-6.
The Mets are 5-2 against first-place Atlanta this season, coming from behind in all five wins. New York has won six of its last seven to climb within 6 1/2 games of the Braves.

Atlanta scored six times in the bottom of the first against All-Star Bobby Jones. But Huskey started the Mets' comeback in the second with a two-run blast off starter Denny Neagle. It came after centre fielder Andruw Jones climbed the fence to rob Bernard Gilkey of a home run.

Huskey added a three-run shot off Neagle in the fourth to lift New York within 6-5, and the Mets tied it one inning later when Manny Alexander hit a leadoff double and scored on second baseman Mark Lemke's error.
New York has won nine of its last 12 one-run games after losing nine of its first 10.
In Chicago, Gary Gaetti and Ray Lankford each blasted three-run homers as the St Louis Cardinals pounded out 20 hits to defeat the Cubs 11-5.
Delino DeShields went 3-for-4 with two RBI and three runs scored, including a solo homer, and Royce Clayton also added three hits for the Cards, who took three of four games from the Cubs.
At Colorado, Quilvio Veras capped a five-run ninth with a bases-clearing double, leading the San Diego Padres to a come-from-behind 13-11 victory over the slumping Rockies.
Colorado's Larry Walker went 3-for-4 with four RBI, raising his major-league leading average to .406.
Padres right fielder Tony Gwynn went 1-for-6 and saw his average fall to .398.
Steve Finley had an RBI triple and a three-run homer for San Diego.
At Florida, Gary Sheffield ignited an eight-run fourth with a solo homer and capped the frame with a three-run shot as the Marlins coasted past the Philadelphia Phillies 9-3.
Sheffield, who became the first Marlin to homer twice in an inning, is the 37th player in major-league history to accomplish the feat.

In Pittsburgh, Kevin Polcovich snapped a tie with an RBI double in the sixth and scored an insurance run in the eighth as the Pirates rallied for a 5-3 victory over the Houston Astros and a split of their four-game series.
The Pirates, who have won nine of their last 11 games, moved one game ahead of second-place Houston in the National League Central.
